verses.1: And when they were all gathered together, they brought him to Pilate.
verses.2: They began to accuse him, saying, “This is what we find strange: our people are scattered and unable to pay taxes to Caesar. Moreover, they claim that he is the king.”
verses.3: And Pilate asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” The man replied, “Yes, I am.”
verses.4: But Pilate said to the priests and the crowd, “I find no reason for any fault in this man.”
verses.5: But those who claimed that Anasai taught the people throughout all of Judea, and that he began his teachings from Galilee all the way down to there.
verses.6: When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
verses.7: And they knew that he had been sent by Herodes to speak with Herodes himself, who was also in Jerusalem on those days.
verses.8: But Herodes, when he saw Jesus, was very pleased. After all, it was time for him to see Him, so that he could hear what He had to say about Himself. He hoped to receive some sign from Him.
verses.9: But he tried to reason with him in a proper manner. But he himself didn’t say anything to him.
verses.10: Then the high priests and the officials began to accuse him equally.
verses.11: And Herodotus also defeated him, along with his army. He surrounded him and sent sharp arrows at him to defeat him.
verses.12: And on that day, Herodotus and Pylades became friends with each other. After all, they had always been enemies before that day.
verses.13: Then Pilate gathered together the priests, the rulers, and the people.
verses.14: He said to them, “Please consider this man as I would consider a person who is about to leave the people. And now, before you, I see that there is no fault in this man that you accuse him of.”
verses.15: But also Herodes sent him to us. And it seems that nothing worthy of death was done to him.
verses.16: So, I will dismiss him from his position.
verses.18: But they were also angry and said, “Let him go! Forgive us, then, for having sent Barabbas away.”
verses.19: Whoever was killed in the city due to some incident, and then killed in prison as well.
verses.20: Once again, Pilate called out to him, wanting to put Jesus to death.
verses.21: And those who cried out said, “Let him be tied in a cross!”
verses.22: The third person said to them, “What evil has this man done? He didn’t find any reason for death in him at all. Therefore, I will dismiss him from his position.”
verses.23: But those who stood up and demanded that he be crucified, and they tried to persuade others to do the same.
verses.24: And Pilate also declared that their question was meaningless.
verses.25: He then released the man who had been imprisoned due to his standing and murder. He also gave Jesus back to them according to their request.
verses.26: And as they captured him, they chose Simon of Cirene, who was coming from the countryside, and ordered him to carry the cross behind Jesus.
verses.27: And a large number of people, both men and women, followed him. They were also very happy to have him with them.
verses.28: But Jesus said to them, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over me. Weep instead for yourselves and for your children.”
verses.29: For days are coming in which the Macarans will be weak and their knees will not function, and those who cannot procreate will also be unable to do so.
verses.30: Then they begin to say to the mountains: “Fall upon us!” And to the hills as well. “Cover us with your shadows!”
verses.31: If this is done in moist wood, what will happen in dry wood?
verses.32: Also, two other wicked people were also to be destroyed along with him.
verses.33: And when we arrived at the place called Kranion, there they crucified him and those who were guilty of evil deeds. One was from the right side, and the other from the left side.
verses.34: But Jesus said, “Father, send them away; they do not know what they are doing.” They then divided up his clothes and distributed them among themselves.
verses.35: And the people began to question him. The rulers also tried to get rid of him by saying, “He saved others; let him save himself. Is this really the Christ of God, the chosen one?”
verses.36: And those soldiers who were approaching him also praised him, offering him their respects.
verses.37: And they said, “If you are indeed the king of the Jews, then save yourself.”
verses.38: And there was also a inscription on it: “This is the king of the Jews.”
verses.39: One of the wicked who were gathered there threatened him, saying, “Are you really the Christ? Then save yourself and us too.”
verses.40: But the other man, after hearing this, said to him: “Do not be afraid of the God, for you are also in His punishment.”
verses.41: And we, certainly, deserve to receive what we have done rightfully. But he did nothing wrong at all.
verses.42: And he said, “Jesus, remember when you went into your kingdom.”
verses.43: And he said to him, “Amun says that today, along with me, you shall be taken to the wilderness.”
verses.44: And already, as the sixth hour began, darkness covered the entire earth until the ninth hour.
verses.45: When the sun went down, the roof of the temple collapsed in the middle.
verses.46: And Jesus said in a loud voice, “Father, I give my spirit into your hands.” And as he said this, he breathed out his spirit.
verses.47: Seeing what was happening, the centurion praised the god, saying, “Indeed, this man was just.”
verses.48: And all those people who were involved in this situation agreed with this view. They considered what was happening and stood up for their beliefs.
verses.49: And all those who knew him from afar stood around him. Women who lived in Galilee also watched these things happen.
verses.50: And I see that there is a man named Joseph, who is a good and just person.
verses.51: He was not in agreement with their decisions and actions. He came from the city of Ermonia, belonging to the Jews. He ruled under the rule of God.
verses.52: When he came before Pilate, he touched Jesus’ body.
verses.53: And he wrapped it up in a shroud, and placed it in a tomb where no one else could lie down.
verses.54: And it was a Friday, and he observed Saturday as well.
verses.55: And they observed the women who had come from Galilee with him. They visited his tomb and saw how his body was laid in it.
verses.56: And they prepared various kinds of spices and perfumes for this occasion. On Saturday, they observed all the rules and regulations as required.
